result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B explains more clearly what a hiring reader needs to see first (the work and decisions up front). It rebuilds the case study around 2–3 decisions with before/after and a result shown only if one exists, and it marks every missing fact as a placeholder for the user to fill in. A is solid and handles the vague title more directly, but its new structure is more generic and less explicit about not making up results. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is better because it rebuilds the case study around specific decisions. It uses clear placeholders, says plainly it won't guess at missing facts, and ends with a precise list of what it needs from the user. B covers nearly the same ground and does better on the vague title, but it leans more on outcomes in general and gives a less concrete list of what the user must supply.
